summary: Request: deterministic ordered audit batches with field normalization and on-demand playback sample
description:
Issue summary:
Atlas Financial reports occasional out-of-order events when ingesting Redwood audit batches into their SIEM. They require deterministic ordering, field canonicalization (timezone and identity mapping), and a small on-demand playback sample bundle to validate their SOC ingestion pipeline.

Impact:
- Customer cannot guarantee forensic ordering for transaction-related audit events in their SIEM, delaying compliance sign-off for a production rollout.
- Manual reordering is brittle and incompatible with their real-time alerting windows.

Request / Desired deliverable:
- Exported audit batches where ordering is deterministic and reproducible (resume tokens + stable sequence number).
- Field normalization mapping doc (timestamp canonicalization to UTC ISO8601, event_server_received_ts, event_sequence_id, tenant_id canonicalization).
- On-demand playback sample (1 hour window) delivered as an signed, resumable S3 manifest with sample events and a small playback harness script (python) that demonstrates resume and deterministic ordering.
- Evidence of HMAC/manifest signing and guidance for KEK rotation for legal chain-of-custody.

Environment:
- Customer: Atlas Financial (enterprise)
- Redwood environment: prod us-east-1, audit-export to customer S3 bucket (s3://atlas-audit-ingest).
- Models referenced in events: redwood-base-1 (generation), redwood-embed-2 (embeddings context).

Steps customer performed to reproduce / validate:
1) Triggered several high-throughput requests to the hosted API from multiple app hosts (simulated load).
2) Requested on-demand audit export for the specified 2026-03-09 14:00-15:00 UTC window.
3) Received NDJSON batches and observed events with non-monotonic timestamps when sorted by event.timestamp vs observed order in SIEM.
4) Manual sort by event_server_received_ts restores chronological order but customer requires native deterministic ordering to remove ambiguity for audit.

Attached logs and artifacts provided by customer:
- s3_manifest_sample.json (manifest listing 2026-03-09 batches)
- sample_event_lines.ndjson (first 500 events)
- screenshot of SIEM ingestion showing reordering

Preferred follow-up: 1:1 customer call to review sample bundle and agree on canonical fields and signing approach.
investigation_notes:
03-10: Initial triage: downloaded customer sample from s3://atlas-audit-ingest (manifest provided). Observed two ordering causes: (1) small clock skew between edge ingress agents and the redwood ingest frontends; (2) microbatch reassembly at export time uses file generation time which can differ from per-event server_received_ts.
Hypothesis: current manifest ordering is by export file creation time rather than deterministic per-event sequence. Proposed fix: include event_sequence_id (server-assigned monotonic int) and event_server_received_ts (RFC3339 UTC) in every exported record and sort by (event_sequence_id) when streaming or building manifests.
Technical notes:
- Candidate changes touch: audit-export pipeline (attachments: exporter manifest generator), s3-delivery lambda to include per-event sequence, and signer to include per-batch HMAC anchored by customer KEK.
- Referenced PR for signer plugin: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2145 (WIP).
- Potential backward-compatibility: include new fields but keep legacy manifest semantics for 30 days.
- Risk: adding per-record sequence numbers will increase manifest size slightly and must be covered by benchmarks for throughput and export time.
resolution_notes:
In Progress — planned actions:
1) Deliver a 1-hour playback sample bundle signed with HMAC and a small playback harness (ETA 2026-03-13).
2) Ship a field-normalization spec (UTC canonicalization, event_sequence_id, event_server_received_ts, tenant hashing guidance) as a Confluence page and example mapping (ETA 2026-03-12).
3) Small infra change to include event_sequence_id in new exports; will be behind feature-flag and rolled out to Atlas Financial's exports first (canary).
Workaround provided to customer: sort incoming events by event_server_received_ts before ingestion into SIEM. Customer accepted workaround for immediate compliance needs.
Follow-ups: schedule a technical review call with Atlas SOC and Platform export engineer (assigned: Marco Diaz) after sample delivery.
